about: Walk-mode bookmarks of the life module. latDeg/lonDeg on the globe as drawn: PALEOMAP paleo-coordinates from 2.6 Ma (where fossils of the listed species cluster, from occurrences.json), modern coordinates below. The camera faces north at local midday; herds are placed by hand at east/north offsets (m) so the view always shows them (approximate, plausible by fossil range and habitat).

sites.title: Late Cretaceous, 66.5 million years ago: Tyrannosaurus, Triceratops and hadrosaurs
sites.source: Hell Creek and Lance formations (Maastrichtian, western North America); paleo-coordinates of their T. rex finds in PBDB are about 47-60 N, 75-85 W

sites.title: Late Jurassic, 150 million years ago: Stegosaurus, sauropods and Allosaurus
sites.source: Morrison Formation (Kimmeridgian-Tithonian, western North America) in paleo-coordinates

sites.title: Late Permian, 252.5 million years ago: pareiasaurs, gorgonopsians and dicynodonts
sites.source: Late Permian of European Russia (Sokolki: Scutosaurus, Inostrancevia, dicynodonts) in paleo-coordinates

sites.title: 3.2 million years ago at Hadar, Ethiopia: Australopithecus ('Lucy') among elephants and giraffes
sites.source: Hadar Formation (A.L. 288-1 'Lucy', 3.18 Ma; Johanson et al. 1978); Africa has moved little since

sites.title: 45,000 years ago on the mammoth steppe: Neanderthals, modern humans, mammoths and horses
sites.source: Mammoth steppe of eastern Europe; Neanderthals until about 40 ka, modern humans in Europe from about 45 ka (Higham et al. 2014)
